==== tluaAssertsWithReturn.tlua (3 errors) ====
    // A signature can assert a parameter and also return values: the return type
    // comes first and `asserts x` (or `asserts x is T`) follows it. Called as a
    // statement it narrows like any assertion; used as a value it returns its type.
    // The lib's `assert` is declared this way.
    
    local function expectString(value: unknown, message: string): string asserts value is string
      if type(value) ~= "string" then
        error(message)
      end
      return value
    end
    
    function statementNarrows(u: unknown): string
      expectString(u, "not a string")
      return u
    end
    
    function valueReturns(u: unknown): string
      local s = expectString(u, "not a string")
      return s
    end

    local function missingReturn(value: unknown): number asserts value

    // A pack return, like the lib's assert.
    local function both(a: string | nil, b: number): (string, number) asserts a
      return assert(a), b
    end
    
    function packNarrows(a: string | nil): string
      both(a, 1)
      return a
    end

    local check = assert
    
    function libAssert(a: string | nil, b: number | nil): number
      assert(a)
      local s: string = a
      check(b, "b is required")
      return b
    end
    
    function libAssertValue(a: string | nil): string
      local s = assert(a)

    // Only a void assertion must be analyzable to be called: one that returns values
    // is still an ordinary call through a table, an element access or _G -- it just
    // does not narrow there.
    declare maybe: string | nil
    local M = { assert = assert }
    M.assert(maybe)
    local fns = { assert }
    fns[1](maybe)
    _G.assert(maybe)
    
    // A never-returning assertion ends flow like any never-returning call.
    declare function die(v: unknown): never asserts v
    
    function dies(y: string | nil): number
      die(y)
    end

    function genericNarrows(u: unknown): number
      checkTag(u, 1)
      return u
